To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GABA-induced currents are inhibited in SCN neurons by Zn2+ and that the sensitivity of these currents to Zn2+ varies during the day and the night.
the zinc sensitivity of the GABAA channels varies with circadian time and that this variation is due to the daily changes in the proportion of the receptors having the gamma subunit.

GABA-evoked current in SCN neurons is sensitive to extracellular zinc, which inhibits the current competitively and in a part, non-competitvely, and that the sensitivity of the receptors to zinc varies during day-night cycle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the circadian variations in the sensitivity of GABAR-channels to zinc, a physiological modulator of GABAergic transmission.
the circadian variations in the GABAergic system in the brain.
the circadian variation in the GABAB receptor function in SCN neurons and provides a novel mechanism for the regulation of circadian rhythms in SCN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SCN GABAA receptors have a higher sensitivity to zinc during the day than during the night.
SCN neurons have two types of GABAA receptors: those with and without the gamma subunit, which are differentially sensitive to zinc and which vary in their proportion during the day and at night.
the SCN neurons have a circadian change in the zinc sensitivity of GABA receptors, which may be related to the daily variations in the expression and/or function of GABAergic system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GABAA receptors of SCN neurons are sensitive to zinc during day and night, and that the sensitivity of the receptors to zinc changes during day and night.
the circadian variations in zinc sensitivity may reflect the daily changes in the proportionality of GABAA receptors with and without gamma subunit.
the GABAergic neurotransmission in the SCN undergoes circadian changes in zinc sensitivity, which could contribute to the circadian rhythm of SCN neuronal activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SCN neurons are more sensitive to zinc during the night, which could be a factor in the circadian regulation of the SCN.
the SCN is enriched with GABAA receptors having gamma subunit, and their proportion changes during day-night cycle.
the circadian clock in the SCN regulates the expression of GABAA receptors with different pharmacological properties.
